title: Finite Tor amplitude of locally constant perfect duals
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p
e\ell$, and let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the admissible condensed coefficient rings $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $A$ is finite commutative and killed by a power of $\ell$ and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$ and $B=\Lambda_S$. Suppose $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ has a pro-étale cover $\{U_i	o S\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] on which it is the termwise scalar extension $B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_i^ ullet}$ of a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], where underlines denote constant sheaves. Form $P^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_B(P,B)$ using relative derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. There exist integers $a\le b$ such that, for every sheaf $N$ of $B$-modules in degree zero,
$$H^q(P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0\quad(q
otin[a,b]),\qquad H^q(P^\vee\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0\quad(q
otin[-b,-a]).$$
In particular both objects have finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For $S=\varnothing$ one can take $a=b=0$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, final sentence (locally constant perfect coefficient dual); paragraph 3, parenthetical assertion that the perfect factors lie in Dctf: extracted uniform-Tor-bound part.

proof.text: Use the module-object/ringed-site derived comparison with $X=S$ and $B=\Lambda_S$. It leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged, identifies relative derived tensor and internal Hom with their ordinary ringed-site versions, and is compatible with slice restriction. We may therefore work throughout with sheaves of modules over the section-ring sheaf of $B$, retaining the notation $B$. In particular the dual in the question is the ringed-site $R\mathcal Hom_B(P,B)$. No replacement of $B$ by the discrete constant sheaf $\underline R$ is made.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); module-object comparison as stated in the cited DAG node

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, all site objects are empty and their empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero, so both required vanishings hold with $a=b=0$. Suppose henceforth $S\ne\varnothing$. Finite type over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives a finite affine open cover of $S$. For each of these affines, the covering condition for $\{U_i\to S\}$ supplies finitely many affine opens in the $U_i$ mapping into that affine and covering it. Combining these finite families gives a finite covering refinement $\{V_j\to S\}_{j\in J}$ subordinate to the original cover. This is a cover by the transitivity axiom of the site. It is nonempty because $S$ is nonempty. On $V_j$, choose the bounded scalar model supplied by its original $U_i$, and choose integers $a_j\le b_j$ outside which that model is zero. Set $a=\min_{j\in J}a_j$ and $b=\max_{j\in J}b_j$. Then $a\le b$ and $[a_j,b_j]\subseteq[a,b]$ for every $j$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, locally constant perfect coefficient dual; finite refinement uses the fpqc covering condition spelled out in def-weil-pbc-proetale-site

proof.text: Write $B_j=B|_{V_j}$ and $E_j^\bullet=B_j\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_j^\bullet}$, so $P|_{V_j}\simeq E_j^\bullet$. The strict-perfect coefficient package gives, in each degree $r$, splittings $F_j^r\xrightarrow{i_r}R^{N_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}F_j^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Its constant-sheaf construction, followed by scalar extension to $B_j$, gives $E_j^r\xrightarrow{I_r}B_j^{N_r}\xrightarrow{P_r}E_j^r$ with $P_rI_r=1$. Scalar extension preserves this equality by functoriality; it need not be exact or flat. Since tensor with $B_j^{N_r}$ is a finite direct sum of the identity, tensor with its retract $E_j^r$ is exact, so $E_j^r$ is flat. Likewise $\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(E_j^r,-)$ is an exact retract of $\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(B_j^{N_r},-)$, which is the finite direct sum functor by the cited finite-free Hom lemma. Exactness passes to these retracts because the corresponding short complex is a direct summand of an exact short complex.

source.place: Section 04TT (section-internal-hom) and Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom): the finite-free Hom calculation is evaluation on the standard basis; Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3). Constant projective splittings are supplied by the cited strict-perfect coefficient package.

proof.text: Derived internal Hom commutes with slice restriction, hence $P^\vee|_{V_j}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(E_j^\bullet,B_j[0])$. By the bounded exact-term Hom lemma, applying $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E_j^\bullet,-)$ to a K-injective resolution $B_j[0]\to I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism: boundedness and the termwise exactness were proved in step 3. By the definition of derived internal Hom, the target computes the displayed derived object. Thus $P^\vee|_{V_j}$ is represented by $D_j^\bullet=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{B_j}(E_j^\bullet,B_j[0])$. Explicitly $D_j^n=\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(E_j^{-n},B_j)$ and $d_{D_j}^n(\phi)=(-1)^{n+1}\phi\circ d_{E_j}^{-n-1}$. In particular $D_j^n=0$ unless $n\in[-b_j,-a_j]$.

source.place: Tag 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); Tag 08JH (lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect), its K-injective comparison; Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes)

proof.text: Applying $\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(-,B_j)$ to the splitting in step 3 exhibits each $D_j^n$ as a retract of $\mathcal Hom_{B_j}(B_j^{N_{-n}},B_j)\cong B_j^{N_{-n}}$: the inclusion is precomposition with $P_{-n}$, the retraction is precomposition with $I_{-n}$, and their composite is precomposition with $P_{-n}I_{-n}=1$. Hence $D_j^n$ is flat by the same finite-direct-sum and retract argument for tensor used in step 3. Apply implication (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of the ringed-site flat-model criterion first to $E_j^\bullet$ in $[a_j,b_j]$ and then to $D_j^\bullet$ in $[-b_j,-a_j]$. For every sheaf $M$ of $B_j$-modules, it gives $H^q(P|_{V_j}\otimes_{B_j}^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ outside $[a_j,b_j]$ and $H^q(P^\vee|_{V_j}\otimes_{B_j}^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ outside $[-b_j,-a_j]$.

source.place: Tag 08JH (lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect), dual terms as in the proof of Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex); Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude), implication (2) to (1)

proof.text: Fix any sheaf $N$ of $B$-modules. Slice restriction is exact, so it commutes with cohomology, and its derived pullback is its termwise restriction. The derived tensor-pullback comparison therefore gives, for $T=P$ and for $T=P^\vee$, $H^q(T\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)|_{V_j}\cong H^q(T|_{V_j}\otimes_{B_j}^{\mathbf L}N|_{V_j})$. Taking $M=N|_{V_j}$ in step 5 shows these restrictions vanish for $q\notin[a,b]$ in the first case and $q\notin[-b,-a]$ in the second, since both local intervals are contained in the corresponding global intervals.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to localization; sites-modules.tex Section 03DH (section-localize), the identity coefficient map and restriction formula, with Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact).

proof.text: The family $\{V_j\}$ covers the final object $S$, so its pullbacks cover every object of the small site. Apply the cover-local isomorphism criterion to the map from each of the cohomology sheaves in step 6 to zero, using underlying abelian sheaves: every slice restriction is an isomorphism to zero, hence the original map is an isomorphism. This proves both global vanishings for the arbitrary sheaf $N$. The same integers $a,b$ were fixed before choosing $N$, and the reflected interval is exactly $[-b,-a]$. By the definition of Tor amplitude these are the asserted finite Tor bounds. The comparison in step 1 transports the vanishings back to module objects without changing their cohomology sheaves.
